title: Underived adjunction and pullback-square normalization at an identity open locus
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. All schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible commutative condensed coefficient [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Use the small pro-etale sites in the coefficient universe, the internal module categories $\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$, and the specified module pullback/direct-image adjunctions $f^*\dashv f_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback, def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. Their pullbacks are exact [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main]. Let $h:D\to Z$, let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and specify $h^{-1}(U)\cong U$ over $U$, with resulting open inclusion $i:U\hookrightarrow D$ and $hi=j$. No properness or density is assumed. Write $c_h:j^*h_*\cong i^*$ for the sectionwise comparison whose value at every pro-etale $T\to U$ is the identity on $M(T\to U\xrightarrow{i}D)$. Write $a_h:i^*h^*\cong j^*$ for the inverse of the composition comparison [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] for $hi=j$, using the canonical identity-pullback identification.

These comparisons are well-defined natural module isomorphisms, with the restricted structural ring action on both sides; on the localized identity morphism $a_h$ is the tensor-unit identification $1\otimes m\mapsto m$. They respect the specified underived adjuncts: for every $M\in\Mod_{\Lambda_Z}$, $N\in\Mod_{\Lambda_D}$ and $t:h^*M\to N$, writing $t^\sharp=h_*t\circ\eta_{h,M}$, one has
$$c_{h,h^*M}\circ j^*(\eta_{h,M})=a_{h,M}^{-1},\qquad c_{h,N}\circ j^*(t^\sharp)=i^*(t)\circ a_{h,M}^{-1}.$$

Let $v:Z'\to Z$, put $D'=D\times_ZZ'$ with maps $h':D'\to Z'$ and $w:D'\to D$, and put $U'=U\times_ZZ'$ with maps $v_U:U'\to U$, $j':U'\hookrightarrow Z'$ and $i':U'\hookrightarrow D'$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Thus $h'^{-1}(U')=U'$ and $h'i'=j'$. Define $a_{h'},c_{h'}$ by the same prescriptions; the two adjunct equations also hold for them. Form the canonical composition comparisons
$$\theta:h'^*v^*\cong w^*h^*,\quad s:j'^*v^*\cong v_U^*j^*,\quad t_0:i'^*w^*\cong v_U^*i^*$$
from [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp], with its specified conjugate normalization [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Then for every $A\in\Mod_{\Lambda_Z}$ the following equality holds, naturally in $A$:
$$t_{0,h^*A}\circ i'^*(\theta_A)\circ a_{h',v^*A}^{-1}=v_U^*(a_{h,A}^{-1})\circ s_A.$$
The same equality holds after termwise application to complexes and passage to the ordinary unbounded derived categories, with precisely these termwise comparisons [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

source.place: Tag 04J0, lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites; explicit adjunction/conjugate normalization for the identity localized map, and the pullback-composition comparison of sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 07A7, remark-base-change.

proof.text: Work on the small sites in the coefficient universe. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1),(4), the sites over the opens $U\subset Z$ and $U\subset D$ are the corresponding slice sites. Replace internal modules by sectionwise modules using [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], which preserves the underlying sheaves and their section maps. The base-change functor $T\mapsto D\times_ZT$ defining $h_*$ is continuous by [def-sfb-finite-lower-star]; it preserves finite limits since both iterated fibre products represent the same tuples with the same equations. On slices over $U$, it becomes the identity: $D\times_ZT\cong T$ for $T\to U$, naturally in $T$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] applies, with the given structural ring map, and identifies restricted direct image with the direct image of this identity localized morphism.

source.place: Tags 04J0 (lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites) and 03CF (sites.tex, lemma-localize-morphism); application to the two open slices

proof.text: The coefficient identifications here are the canonical ones, not arbitrary ring isomorphisms. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1), use $j^{-1}\Lambda_Z\cong\Lambda_U$ and $i^{-1}\Lambda_D\cong\Lambda_U$. Apply [lem-sfb-eta-comp] to $U\xrightarrow{i}D\xrightarrow{h}Z$: the coefficient map for $j=hi$ is the coefficient map for $h$ followed by that for $i$, with the specified pushforward composition. Therefore the localized structural map, expressed in these two copies of $\Lambda_U$, is the identity. In particular, the direct-image comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] is exactly $c_h$: on $T\to U$ it is $N(D\times_ZT)=N(T\xrightarrow{i}D)$. The same equality holds for every restriction map and for multiplication by a section of the restricted ring. This proves that $c_h$ is a natural module isomorphism and fixes its action, including its direction.

source.place: Tag 04J0, restricted structural ring map and sectionwise direct-image identity; coefficient composition for hi=j

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-ringed-site-pullback-localization-universes] to the same base-change functor and its slice at $U$. The finite-limit and continuity hypotheses were checked in step 1; slice continuity is also supplied by the induced morphism in [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism]. The global left adjoint is the specified $h^*$, by [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. The localized adjunction is that for the identity ringed site. Its pullback is $R\otimes_R-$, $R=\Lambda_U$, with unit $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ and counit $r\otimes n\mapsto rn$: these are the two Hom correspondences in [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction] when the underlying site functor and ring map are identities. They are inverse under $R\otimes_RM\cong M$. The localization lemma consequently gives an isomorphism $d_M:j^*M\to i^*h^*M$ with $d_M=c_{h,h^*M}\,j^*\eta_{h,M}$. In localized tensor coordinates $d_M(m)=1\otimes m$.

source.place: Tag 04J0, localized module pullback with its restricted-unit Hom correspondence

proof.text:
Identify $d$ with the comparison required by the statement. Write $b:j^*\to i^*h^*$ for the forward comparison of [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] for $hi=j$. Its conjugate is the specified $C:h_*i_*\to j_*$ of [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp]. The defining unit equation of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation], with $L_1=j^*$ and $L_2=i^*h^*$, is
$$j_*(b_M)\eta_{j,M}=C_{i^*h^*M}\,h_*(\eta_{i,h^*M})\,\eta_{h,M}.$$
Here the second unit is the composite unit of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Evaluate this equation at an object $T\to U$. For an open, restriction to its own slice makes its unit the identity under the tensor-unit identification, by the identity-site calculation in step 3 (applied also to $i$ and $j$). The map $C$ evaluates by the canonical fibre-product identification of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp]; on this slice it is the identity. The displayed equation is therefore $b_M(T)=c_{h,h^*M}(T)\,j^*\eta_{h,M}(T)=d_M(T)$. This holds on every object and restriction map, so $b=d$. Since $a_h=b^{-1}$ by definition, $a_h$ is exactly $1\otimes m\mapsto m$, and $c_{h,h^*M}\,j^*\eta_{h,M}=a_{h,M}^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 03D8, lemma-push-pull-composition-modules; explicit comparison of the localized unit with the conjugate-normalized composition

proof.text: For $t:h^*M\to N$, use the definition $t^\sharp=h_*t\,\eta_{h,M}$. Naturality of the sectionwise comparison gives $c_{h,N}\,j^*h_*t=i^*t\,c_{h,h^*M}$. Compose this equation with $j^*\eta_{h,M}$ and insert step 4. This is exactly $c_{h,N}\,j^*(t^\sharp)=i^*t\,a_{h,M}^{-1}$. It proves the adjunct formula for the specified adjunction, not just for an isomorphic choice of adjunction.

source.place: Tag 04J0; naturality of the comparison followed by the unit equality proved in step 4

proof.text: By the defining fibre-product identities [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], $(D\times_ZZ')\times_{Z'}U'\cong D\times_ZU'\cong U'$, with the second isomorphism induced by the fixed identity locus. Thus $h'$ has the same identity-open configuration, with $h'i'=j'$. All primed schemes are standing schemes, all maps are the specified base changes, and the site sizes remain in the coefficient universe. Repeat steps 1--5 with $(h',i',j')$ to obtain $c_{h'},a_{h'}$ and both primed adjunct equations. This argument uses no properness or density; in particular it makes no assumption that density survives base change.

source.place: Tag 04J0; base change of the identity localized morphism

proof.text:
For clarity write $m_{f,g}:f^*g^*\to(gf)^*$ for the inverse of the specified pullback composition. These comparisons satisfy
$$m_{f,qg}\,f^*m_{g,q}=m_{gf,q}\,(m_{f,g}q^*).$$
Indeed [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] makes each $m$ the conjugate of inverse direct-image composition. On a site object $T$, both ways to compare three direct images are induced, by [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp], by the same map from an iterated fibre product to the unparenthesized fibre product: they preserve $T$ and each of the three other projections. The universal property makes these maps equal, and [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp] lifts them to the same module morphism. The specified coefficient actions agree since both act through the same composite ring map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2),(3) and the injective conjugation bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]; the two conjugates of the displayed equation are precisely those equal direct-image maps. Thus the displayed associativity identity holds with the composite-adjunction normalization, including the functor associators.

source.place: Tag 03D8; associativity obtained by conjugating the sectionwise direct-image associativity

proof.text:
The common composite is $q=vh'i'=hwi'=jv_U:U'\to Z$. Use the notation of step 7, and suppress only canonical equality transports. By definition
$$\theta=m_{w,h}^{-1}m_{h',v},\quad s=m_{v_U,j}^{-1}m_{j',v},\quad t_0=m_{v_U,i}^{-1}m_{i',w},\quad a_h=m_{i,h},\quad a_{h'}=m_{i',h'}.$$
Apply step 7 to the triple $(i',h',v)$: since $h'i'=j'$, it gives
$$i'^*m_{h',v}\,(m_{i',h'}v^*)^{-1}=m_{i',vh'}^{-1}m_{j',v}.$$
For $(i',w,h)$ it gives
$$m_{i',w}h^*\,i'^*m_{w,h}^{-1}=m_{wi',h}^{-1}m_{i',hw}.$$
Insert these into $t_0\,i'^*\theta\,a_{h'}^{-1}$ and cancel $m_{i',hw}m_{i',vh'}^{-1}$, since $hw=vh'$. The result is
$$m_{v_U,i}^{-1}h^*\,m_{iv_U,h}^{-1}m_{j',v}.$$
Finally step 7 for $(v_U,i,h)$ and $hi=j$ rewrites this as
$$v_U^*(m_{i,h}^{-1})\,m_{v_U,j}^{-1}m_{j',v}=v_U^*(a_h^{-1})\,s.$$
This is the claimed square equality, with all components evaluated at $A$. Each operation used natural transformations, so it is natural in $A$.

source.place: Tag 03D8 and sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change); explicit reassociation around the two paths U′→Z

proof.text: All transformations in the square equation involve composites of pullbacks. They are additive exact functors by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main], so their termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms and induce the ordinary unbounded derived pullbacks of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], by the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Naturality makes their degreewise components commute with every differential. The equality in step 8 is therefore an equality of chain maps, and applying localization at quasi-isomorphisms preserves it. This proves precisely the stated derived square equality with the same termwise comparisons. No descent of the generally nonexact underived $h_*$ is used.

tool_uses.why: Generic pro-etale localization, identifying open sites with slices; no node of the composition unit supplies this site equivalence.

Generic module localization comparison with restricted adjunction unit in the coefficient universe; the composition unit does not state this normalized local Hom correspondence.
Generic composition formula for the pulled-back coefficient structural maps, fixing the localized ring action.
